JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION A:
Jermaine Jackson
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0117 | jermaine.jackson@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Financial analyst in hospital FP&A with seven years of experience in budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis. Builds detailed Excel models that department leaders rely on every month, and over the past year has started pulling some data with SQL and sharing a few results in Tableau. Looking to move from financial planning into operational analytics with more hands-on BI work.

EXPERIENCE
Financial Analyst, FP&A | Linden Park Medical Center, Columbus, OH | Jan 2022 to Present
• Prepare monthly budget variance reports for 22 cost centers in surgery, imaging, laboratory and support services, about $310M in annual operating expense.
• Built the department level annual budget model in Excel with driver tabs for patient volume, staffing and supply cost per case; finance leadership adopted it for the 2025 and 2026 budget cycles.
• Write variance commentary for the CFO's monthly operating review and meet with department directors to walk through any line that moves more than 5 percent.
• Write SQL each week against the financial data mart to pull general ledger, payroll and supply charge detail, mostly by adjusting queries written by the decision support team and adding joins and date filters.
• Built a Tableau dashboard on supply cost per case by surgical service, shared with supply chain leaders ahead of the quarterly spend review.
• Modeled the cost impact of a proposed overtime policy change, showing about $1.1M in annual savings; the change was approved after review by nursing and HR leadership.
• Traced a jump in laboratory supply expense to a vendor item that had been mapped to the wrong cost center in the data mart, and worked with decision support to correct six months of history.
• Support the annual capital budget by tracking 150 equipment requests, vendor quotes and approval status in a shared workbook.
• Answer weekly questions from department managers about staffing variances and supply charges, usually by email with a short Excel attachment.
• Rebuilt the rolling 12 month forecast template so that monthly updates take one day instead of three.

Accounting Analyst | Arbor Surgical Supply, Columbus, OH | Jul 2019 to Dec 2021
• Handled month end close tasks for a medical supply distributor: accruals, inventory reserve calculations and balance sheet reconciliations.
• Built a gross margin by customer report in Excel that the sales director used in quarterly pricing conversations.
• Reconciled inventory between the ERP and the warehouse management system each month and documented recurring timing differences.
• Prepared freight cost analysis by carrier that supported renegotiation of two shipping contracts.
• Assisted with the annual physical inventory count and the reconciliation of count variances.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2019

SKILLS
Excel: financial modeling, XLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH, pivot tables, Power Query, scenario tables, basic macros
Data: SQL (joins, aggregation, date filters), Epic financial reports, Oracle ERP
BI: Tableau Desktop (basic dashboards), PowerPoint for executive summaries
Finance: budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, cost per case, month end close, account reconciliation
Healthcare: payer mix, patient volume statistics, labor productivity reporting

ADDITIONAL
• Took a six week evening SQL class, 2024
• Member of a local healthcare finance association chapter, attending monthly education sessions
• Volunteer bookkeeping support for a neighborhood food pantry, preparing quarterly budget summaries
